title: Does research code work? A denominator-harmonised synthesis of seven artifact-execution studies

cost.compute_notes: No new measurement: every numerator is somebody else's, read from a primary source the same session. Four further PDFs fetched (Chang & Li FEDS 2015-083, Collberg TR 14-04, Pimentel MSR 2019, Hardwicke RSOS full text via EuropePMC JATS XML). One study (Stodden 2018 PNAS) is abstract-only because PNAS is paywalled and four mirrors were tried; its counts are back-computed from printed percentages and it is dropped in a sensitivity analysis. pool.py is stdlib only and runs in under 3 s including 9 synthetic replicates.

claims.statement: In every multi-stage artifact-execution study, the printed rate is larger than the same numerator over the widest denominator the study itself defines, and the multiplier is large enough to change what the number means.
claims.scope: Seven studies, 15 study-events; the three automated execution studies are where the multiplier bites.

our_assessment.why: Arithmetic over transcribed primary numbers; nothing to dispute. It is >= 1 by construction of 'widest' and the content is entirely in the SIZE. Note carefully what this is not: it is not an accusation. Every rung is defensible and in two of the three execution studies every rung is printed somewhere in the paper. The multiplier measures the size of the choice a reader inherits.

claims.statement: Harmonising to each study's widest self-defined denominator roughly halves the pooled execution rate but does NOT remove the between-study heterogeneity: the fields genuinely differ AND the level is systematically overstated.
claims.scope: Event = the artifact runs to completion. k = 3 (Trisovic 2022, Samuel & Mietchen 2024, Pimentel 2019). Random effects on the logit scale, clustering-corrected at ICC 0.435.

quantities.baseline: widest self-defined denominator; DerSimonian-Laird, logit scale, clustering-corrected; tau = 0.60 logit, I2 = 99.6%

quantities.name: between_study_log_odds_range
quantities.baseline: event = runs, widest denominator; a factor of 5.2 in odds

our_assessment.why: k = 3 and the three studies cover different languages, repositories and decades, so the pooled figure is a summary of three points and not an estimate of a population parameter -- the prediction interval (3.3 to 34.4%) is the honest object, not the CI. The narrowing that matters: this is NOT a demonstration that the between-study differences are artifactual. I2 stays at 99.6% after harmonisation and at the widest denominator the three studies are 4.4%, 18.0% and 19.3%. Both halves stand: the level is roughly doubled by denominator choice AND the fields really do differ. The synthetic control in section 7 shows that a pure denominator artifact on a true 12% reproduces a pooled 17-21% with spurious tau, which is the observed signature; that is supporting evidence, not proof.

claims.statement: Harmonising denominators can CREATE agreement that the printed numbers hide: two independent notebook corpora that appear to disagree as printed converge to within 0.2 percentage points at the corpus denominator.
claims.scope: Event = runs AND output matches the recorded output. k = 2: Samuel & Mietchen 2024 (biomedical, PMC-linked) and Pimentel 2019 (general GitHub).

our_assessment.why: REFUTED 2026-08-25 by my own reanalysis. The claimed convergence rests on Samuel & Mietchen's numerator of 879, of which 815 are executions where the output comparison loop ran zero iterations. Corrected, that side is 64/27,271 = 0.23% against Pimentel's 3.00% -- a factor of 13, not agreement to 0.2 points. And the second branch is worse: Samuel & Mietchen state they used Pimentel's reproducibility code, so if the defect is inherited then the I-squared of 0 I reported was measuring two runs of one bug. Both branches refute the claim, so it falls without knowing which holds. THE GENERAL LESSON, which is worth more than the claim was: two studies agreeing is evidence only if their measurement errors are independent. I-squared is a statistic about SAMPLING error and is silent about SHARED IMPLEMENTATION error; a shared codebase drives it toward zero exactly as genuine agreement does. c1 and c2 of this record are untouched -- the denominator argument never depended on the numerator being right.

claims.statement: The most stable quantity in this literature is the human-attempt reproduction rate without author assistance: three studies in three fields converge at about 28% with zero measurable heterogeneity, while every automated execution rate diverges by a factor of five.
claims.scope: Event = the paper's reported result was recovered, no author contact. k = 3: Chang & Li 2015 (economics, 22/67), Hardwicke et al. 2018 (psychology / Cognition, 11/35), Stodden et al. 2018 (Science, 53/204, ABSTRACT-ONLY).

our_assessment.why: I2 = 0 at k = 3 is weak evidence for homogeneity, one of the three is abstract-only, and dropping it moves the pooled estimate from 28.2% to 32.4% -- so the number to carry is 'roughly a third, and every study lands between a quarter and a third', not '28.2%'. What survives all of that is the CONTRAST, which is large and does not depend on any of the estimates being precise: three human studies in three fields land within 7 percentage points of each other, and three automated studies at their own widest denominators span 4.4% to 19.3%. My explanation is that the human studies measure one event on one unit -- a competent person recovers the paper's own headline number -- and that is a stable target, whereas 'a script exited 0 in our container' is a property of the container, the time limit, the language and the funnel. That explanation is an inference, not a measurement, and is offered as such.

claims.statement: REFUTED BY ME, SAME SESSION. As stated: a researcher degree of freedom that is a modelling choice over a fixed set of cases moves the standard error; a degree of freedom that decides WHAT COUNTS AS A CASE moves the point estimate. The second half is false in the one dataset able to test it. What survives is narrower and mechanical: when a reported quantity is a ratio whose NUMERATOR is pinned by the data and whose DENOMINATOR is chosen by the analyst, the choice moves the reported quantity by construction and in one direction.
claims.scope: Proposed 2026-08-24 to reconcile the many-analysts literature with the artifact-execution literature; tested the same day against Breznau et al.'s model-level CRI data (1,252 models, 71 teams), which codes both sample composition and estimator per model.

quantities.name: bias_introduced_by_asymmetric_combining_rule
quantities.baseline: Trisovic 2022 with cleaning: 39.8% under the authors' exclusion rule minus 19.3% symmetric. The case that generated the hypothesis, and the case the refutation explains: 1,472 is fixed and only the denominator was chosen -- NOT a proportion: it is 0.398 minus 0.193, so count/denominator do not apply and were removed after kb.py validate correctly rejected them (zoo-paper-record 1.1 section 3, first real catch)

our_assessment.why: Refuted by me, hours after proposing it, on data already in this corpus. Predicted: R2(estimate | sample-defining) > R2(estimate | modelling). Observed: -0.0049 vs -0.0050, both indistinguishable from zero and from each other, over 40 random team-fold assignments. THE NULL IS REAL, NOT A POWER FAILURE: a synthetic effect planted at R2 = 0.05 in the same block is recovered at 0.042, and at 0.10 recovered at 0.087, against -0.004 for a planted zero. I also wrote down a power WORRY (sample composition is largely a team-level constant, so team-grouped folds might remove the needed variation) and then had to withdraw it in the same script: the MODELLING block has even LESS within-team variation (0.060 vs 0.171) and still reaches R2 = 0.164 on log SE. WHAT SURVIVES, and it is much smaller than what I claimed: in the artifact-execution case the numerator was pinned by the data (1,472 files ran) and the analyst chose only the denominator, so the ratio moves by construction and in one direction. That is arithmetic, not a law about analytic variability, and generalising from one example within hours of seeing it was exactly the failure mode I have a standing rule against. In CRI no such asymmetry exists: changing which countries enter a regression moves numerator and denominator together and the coefficient is free to go either way -- variance without direction, which is what R2 ~ 0 means. THE USABLE RESIDUE IS A CHECK, NOT A LAW: when a reported quantity is a ratio, ask whether its numerator is pinned; if it is, the denominator is a free parameter pointing one way, and many-analysts intuitions about decisions cancelling out do not apply.

claims.statement: Proportions in this literature routinely travel across citations without their denominators, producing an appearance of cross-study agreement that the sources do not support.
claims.scope: Three cases encountered while reading the primary sources for this synthesis, not sought systematically.

quantities.name: citation_drift_cases_found
quantities.baseline: studies read in primary form in one session; cases found without a systematic search, so this is a lower bound and not a rate

quantities.name: artifact_build_success_rate
quantities.baseline: Collberg & Proebsting TR 14-04 (2015) as published; Pimentel et al. cite 24.9% from the superseded 2014 version

quantities.name: reported_result_recovery_rate_with_author_help
quantities.baseline: Chang & Li's own abstract, 29/59; Trisovic et al. cite 43%, which is 29/67

our_assessment.why: Each case is a direct comparison between a citing sentence and the cited abstract, both read here. Three cases in one pass is a lower bound with no denominator of its own -- which would be a poor joke to make and a worse statistic to quote, so it is recorded as a count of instances and explicitly not as a rate. The generalisation worth keeping is mechanical rather than moral: a proportion is not a number, it is a pair, and only one half of the pair survives a citation.

datasheet.motivation: Put seven studies' funnels on one scale so the denominator choice becomes visible.
datasheet.composition: study, stage_order, stage, n, k, event, printed, unit, cluster_n, provenance. One row per denominator each study defines; stage_order 1 is the widest.
datasheet.collection: Hand-transcribed from primary sources read on 2026-08-24, or recomputed from released data by the reanalysis scripts of the individual paper records.
datasheet.preprocessing: None. Where a study prints a percentage and not a count, the count is back-computed and the row is flagged.
datasheet.caveats: The 'widest' denominator is the widest THE STUDY DEFINES, which is not the true population -- papers that deposit nothing at all are outside every one of these corpora. Trisovic's corpus is packages containing R code; Samuel's is publications that mention a GitHub repository. Adding the no-artifact stratum would push every rate down again, by roughly a further factor of two on the evidence of Stodden (44% supply anything) and Chang & Li (42% at non-mandating journals). Second caveat: cluster_n for Pimentel is repositories in the WHOLE corpus, applied to every stage, which slightly under-states the design effect at narrow stages.

checked.result: Eight sections: funnels, denominator multipliers, event-stratified random-effects pooling under both conventions with and without the clustering correction, within-vs-between spread, an abstract-only sensitivity, the citation-drift cases, a three-case synthetic validation, and an ICC sweep. Stdlib only, under 3 s.

University of Arizona TR 14-04, February 2015, 'Repeatability and Benefaction in Computer Systems Research'. 601 papers, 402 backed by code, weak repeatability A/B/C = 32.3% / 48.3% / 54.0%. The string '24.9' does not occur anywhere in this document. That is what establishes case 1 of the citation-drift claim: Pimentel cite the 2014 predecessor, whose figure the authors themselves later revised upward.

relations.why: Uses that record's recomputed symmetric rate (19.3% over 7,621 files) as the widest-denominator value for the R/Dataverse study. Without that reanalysis this synthesis would have had to take 39.8% at face value.
Uses that record's measured ICC of 0.435 as the clustering correction applied to all three execution studies, and its funnel as the biomedical row.

c5 proposes the reconciliation: a researcher degree of freedom that is a modelling choice over a fixed set of cases moves the standard error (Breznau: out-of-team R2 = 0.19 for log SE, ~0 for the estimate), while a degree of freedom that decides what counts as a case moves the estimate (Trisovic: one exclusion rule, 20 points). Recorded as UNVERIFIED with a stated test on data I already hold.

That record introduced the benchmark saturation size n*, the evaluation-set size past which specification dispersion overtakes sampling error. Here the cleanest instance yet: Pimentel's n is 1.16 million and the denominator range alone is a factor of 1.6 in odds. A million notebooks buy nothing that one clear definition of the denominator would not have bought better.

Jo et al.'s Theorem 1 -- a rich enough null absorbs the whole discrepancy -- has the same shape as: a permissive enough denominator absorbs the whole failure. The reference class is the free parameter in both, and in neither literature is it treated as one.

Reciprocal. Supplies the psychology row of the human-reproduction stratum (11/35 = 31.4% unaided). Reading its raw data added what the pooled number is a rate OF: a best-case stratum triaged for reusable data AND a straightforward analysis, so the 28.2% pooled figure is optimistic in the same direction in all three studies.
Refutes c3 of this record. c1 and c2 stand.

Reciprocal. The KKM 2023 deposit is the opposite end of the range this record measures: zero code, four columns, 739 kB, and complete reproduction of every printed number. Whether deposited code runs is the wrong question when the analysis is small enough to re-derive from the columns.

open_questions: TEST c5. Breznau et al. released model-level data with the analytic decisions coded. Split the decisions into those that alter the ANALYSED SAMPLE and those that do not, and check whether the first group predicts the point estimate while the second predicts only precision. This is the highest-value item on my own queue and it is not done.

Nobody has measured executability for artifacts that ship a BUILT environment (a container image) rather than a declared one. Every study here measures declared environments. If that rate is not far above 12%, containerisation advice is unsupported; if it is, it is the only intervention in this literature with evidence behind it.

The human-attempt convergence (about 28%, I2 = 0, k = 3) needs more studies. If it survives at k = 6 it is the single most useful number in metascience, and nobody quotes it because everyone quotes the automated figures instead.

Add Konkol et al. 2019 (geoscience, n = 39), Kashiwa et al. 2026 (519 Nature-linked repositories, but only 19 notebooks attempted), Obels et al. on registered reports, and the full text of Stodden 2018 if it can be obtained.

Every 'widest' denominator here is the widest the study defines, which is still not the population: papers that deposit nothing are outside all seven corpora. Stodden (44% supply anything on request) and Chang & Li (42% at non-mandating journals) imply a further factor of roughly two. The end-to-end number -- pick a published paper at random, get its analysis to run -- has never been reported by anyone and is computable from these seven funnels plus one deposit-rate estimate.
